f.title: Use the RSI as the basis for expectedness assessment for SUSAR reporting and annual safety reporting

rows.quote: The Reference Safety Information (RSI) should be used as the basis for expectedness assessment of Serious Adverse Reactions (SARs) by the sponsor for expedited reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions (SUSARs) and for annual safety reporting.

f.title: Restrict expected SARs in the RSI to SARs observed more than once with the IMP
f.statement: The expected SARs listed in the RSI should be restricted to SARs that have been observed more than once during treatment with the investigational medicinal product (IMP).
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Annex III section 2.2 point 6

rows.quote: The RSI contains expected SARs which should be restricted to SARs that have been observed more than once during treatment with the Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP; see Question 7.9).

f.title: Include an expected SAR only with reasonable evidence of a causal relationship after thorough sponsor assessment
f.statement: For a SAR to be listed as expected in the RSI, there should be reasonable evidence of a causal relationship between the event and IMP treatment, after a thorough assessment by the sponsor. The evidence should be based on, for example, the comparative incidence of SARs in all previous and ongoing clinical trials and a thorough causality evaluation of the individual reported case. The evaluation should be made from events previously observed with the IMP, not from what might be anticipated from its pharmacological properties.
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Annex III section 2.2 point 6

rows.quote: Additionally, after a thorough assessment by the sponsor, reasonable evidence of a causal relationship between the event and the IMP treatment should exist. This evidence should be based on, for example, the comparative incidence of other SARs in all previous and ongoing Clinical Trials (CTs) and on a thorough evaluation of the causality of the individual reported case. The evaluation should be performed from the perspective of events previously observed with the IMP treatment, not based on what might be anticipated from the pharmacological properties of the IMP
rows.review_note: Review: legal_basis set to Annex III 2.2 point 6; the last sentence restates point 6, the causal-evidence test is the Q&A addition. Double-check: quote proves the statement; level, actor and classification correct.

f.title: Do not include single-occurrence SARs in the RSI unless strongly plausible and robustly justified
f.statement: SARs that have occurred only once do not usually qualify for inclusion in the RSI. They may be included only where there is a very strong plausibility of a causal relationship with the IMP and a robust justification based on medical judgement is provided. Biological plausibility from the mechanism of action and the presence of risk-mitigation strategies are not sufficient on their own.
f.exceptions: Very strong plausibility of a causal relationship with the IMP and a robust justification based on medical judgement.

rows.quote:
SARs that have occurred only once do not usually qualify for inclusion in the RSI, unless there is a very strong plausibility of a causal relationship with the IMP and a robust justification based on medical judgement is provided. mitigation strategies alone are not sufficient.

f.title: The originator RSI may be used for a biosimilar if adequately justified
f.statement: The RSI of the originator product may be accepted for a biosimilar product if adequately justified.
f.applicability: Development of biosimilar products

rows.quote: The Reference Safety Information (RSI) of the originator may be accepted for a biosimilar product, if adequately justified.

f.title: Include protocol measures for originator risks and new biosimilar risks
f.statement: For a biosimilar trial, the protocol should include measures to mitigate both the known risks of the originator and any new risks of the biosimilar, such as a potential risk of reduced efficacy compared with the originator.
f.applicability: Development of biosimilar products
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote: In addition, the protocol should include measures to mitigate both the known risks associated with the originator and any new risks associated with the biosimilar (for example potential risk of reduced efficacy when compared with the originator).

f.title: Assess follow-up reports against the RSI in effect when the SAR occurred
f.statement: Expectedness for follow-up reports should be assessed against the RSI that was in effect and approved at the time the SAR occurred.
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Annex III section 2.2 point 8
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote: The Reference Safety Information (RSI) in effect and approved at the time of occurrence of the Serious Adverse Reaction (SAR) should also be used to assess expectedness for follow up reports to cases.

f.title: Do not downgrade a SUSAR because the RSI was updated after the event
f.statement: A SUSAR should not be downgraded on the ground that the RSI was updated after the event occurred.
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Annex III section 2.2 point 8
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) should not be downgraded on the basis that the RSI was updated after the occurrence of an event.
